clue.text: Prosper after promotion and leave the rest behind!

indicators.note: after places the word for prosper behind the other pieces

parts.note: a promotion at work is a rise
taken as written
to prosper or excel is to shine

explanation.surface: Someone does well after being promoted and leaves the others behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheery wake-up call tells a sleeper to get up and leave their rest behind; an idiom for waking.

clue.text: Church feature restored badly, as short of time

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of restored are rearranged

explanation.surface: A church ornament was poorly restored because the work was rushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' removes T from RESTORED; 'badly' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen behind a church altar, a typical feature of a church.

clue.text: Officer needing great home to finish up in temporary shelter

parts.note: super means great or excellent
in means at home

indicators.note: in places the word for finish inside the shelter

parts.note: a tent is a temporary shelter
to finish up is to end

explanation.surface: A police officer needs a great house and ends up sleeping in a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A superintendent is a senior police officer rank in Britain, above chief inspector.

clue.text: Record girl as having left

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl's departure goes down in the records.
explanation.definitionFit: An annal is a record of a single year's events, usually in the plural for historical records.

clue.text: One gets to delay goal going in?

definitions.text: One gets to delay goal going in?

indicators.note: going in means the word for goal is placed inside

parts.note: to delay is to defer
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A footballer manages to hold up a goal that is about to go in.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a picture of a footballer's job: holding up a goal that is about to go in.
explanation.definitionFit: A defender's role in football is to stop or delay goals going in; the clue describes that role.

clue.text: Host only offering some another drink

indicators.note: offering some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A host offers a guest just a little of a second drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a great number, as is a herd, a crowd of people or animals; a synonym.

clue.text: You can just make out something here by fielder

definitions.text: You can just make out something here

parts.note: by means near, as in standing by
point is a cricket fielding position square of the batsman on the off side

explanation.surface: A spectator can barely see something next to a cricket fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a sport played across Britain, point is a fielder; the near point is the closest distance at which the eye can focus.
explanation.definitionFit: The near point is the closest point at which an eye can bring an object into focus, the limit of seeing.

clue.text: Vain schemer surprisingly holding off smarmy campaign

indicators.note: holding means the rearranged letters hold the next word inside them
surprisingly signals the letters of the two preceding words are mixed into an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A conceited plotter unexpectedly drops an oily public relations drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' scrambles the first two words; 'holding' then wraps those mixed letters round the word off, splitting them after the fifth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm offensive is a calculated campaign of flattery and friendliness to win people over, hence smarmy.

clue.text: A brief description of Abraham's grave?

parts.note: Abraham came from Ur of the Chaldees, so Ur is Abraham's home city
gent is a brief word for a gentleman, a description of the man

explanation.surface: The clue pretends to ask for a short epitaph on Abraham's tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a burial place but is the adjective; a man from Ur is an Ur gent.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and urgent both describe a serious, pressing situation that demands attention.

clue.text: Inscription paid for by minster

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the classic gravestone inscription
if drinks are on someone they are paid for by them

explanation.surface: A memorial inscription has been funded by the local church.
explanation.walkthrough: RIPON is a cathedral city in North Yorkshire whose cathedral was long known as Ripon Minster.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripon's great church is traditionally called a minster, so the city is identified by it; a metonymic example.

clue.text: Meet dad outside party that finishes early

indicators.note: outside says the word for dad goes round the shortened party

parts.note: dad is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: a word that finishes early has lost its last letter

parts.note: an orgy is a wild party

explanation.surface: Arrange to see your father somewhere other than a party that ends ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that finishes early' drops the party word's last letter; 'outside' wraps the word for dad round what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgather is an old verb meaning to assemble or gather together, a synonym of meet.

clue.text: Beloved embracing king with the lights out

indicators.note: embracing means the word for beloved holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a beloved person is a darling
K is the abbreviation for king in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A lover holds a monarch close in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Darkling is a poetic word meaning in the dark, which is where you are with the lights switched off.

clue.text: Plant with sulphur needing decontamination

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
a purge is a cleansing or decontamination

explanation.surface: A plant needs sulphur to clean it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurge is a common plant of the genus Euphorbia, with milky sap; an example of a plant.

clue.text: Relation embracing fashionable Left

indicators.note: embracing means the relative holds the next piece inside

parts.note: a sister is a family relation
in means fashionable, as in the in thing

explanation.surface: A relative hugs someone stylish who has just departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb, departed, but it is the direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister is the Latin and heraldic word for the left-hand side, as opposed to dexter.

clue.text: Rascal entertained by composer no end, company being congenial

indicators.note: entertained by means the rascal is held inside the shortened composer
no end means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Erik Satie was a French composer
an imp is a mischievous child or rascal

explanation.surface: A rogue is welcomed by a composer endlessly, and the company is friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' drops the composer's last letter; 'entertained by' puts the rascal inside what is left, and company follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Simpatico, borrowed from Italian and Spanish, means likeable and easy to get on with.

clue.text: I travel in place and overindulge

indicators.note: in says the first pieces sit inside the word for place

parts.note: to place something is to put it
to travel is to go

explanation.surface: Someone moves about a venue and eats too much.
explanation.definitionFit: To pig out is an informal idiom for eating greedily, which is to overindulge.

clue.text: Drink lots of alcohol (litre) fair entertainment?

parts.note: to carouse is to drink heavily and make merry

explanation.surface: Downing a litre of booze is fine entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' looks like an adjective meaning reasonable, but it is the funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousel is a merry-go-round, a ride found at a funfair; hence the question mark.

clue.text: Dull male not right romantic

indicators.note: male not right means one letter for male stands where the letter for right was

parts.note: dull means dreary

explanation.surface: A boring man is said to be wrong for romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' swaps R for M in DREARY: one R gives way to M.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamy describes someone romantic and wistful, lost in pleasant fancies; a synonym.

clue.text: Show out-of-date record in short Oxford book?

indicators.note: in places the record inside the book

parts.note: dict is short for dictionary, and Oxford is famed for its dictionary
an EP, extended play, is an old-fashioned record format

explanation.surface: An old record is displayed inside an abbreviated Oxford volume.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict is to show or represent in a picture or words; a synonym.

clue.text: Dogs fight when in large group

indicators.note: when in places the quarrel inside the large group

parts.note: a mass is a large group
a tiff is a minor fight or quarrel

explanation.surface: Dogs scrap with one another when gathered in a pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastiffs are a large, powerful breed of dog, so the plural is an example of dogs.

clue.text: Tempting old instrument?

parts.note: the creature that tempted Eve in Eden was the devil's instrument, and the same word names an old wind instrument

explanation.surface: A seductive antique musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eden tempter was a snake, and a snaking bass wind instrument of old bore that name.

clue.text: One said to be wheeler dealer?

indicators.note: said to be means the word is spoken and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: a wheeler, one who turns wheels, is a pedaller on a bicycle

explanation.surface: A man is thought to be a wheeler-dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheeler dealer' reads as one shady phrase, but the clue splits it: wheeler is the cyclist, dealer the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedlar is a travelling trader who sells small goods, so he is a kind of dealer.

clue.text: Our current epoch lacks a certain type of undergraduate

indicators.note: lacks means a letter is dropped from the phrase for our epoch

parts.note: the present calendar era is the Common Era, CE

explanation.surface: Modern times are short of a particular kind of student.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford a commoner is an undergraduate without a scholarship or exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford and some colleges, a student not on a scholarship is called by this term; a university-specific sense.

clue.text: Religious figure will be seen in. "places of worship, no question

indicators.note: no means the abbreviation for question is removed

parts.note: mosques are Muslim places of worship

explanation.surface: A religious leader appears in houses of worship without being challenged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be seen in' looks like a hidden-word signal but is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Moses is the prophet who led the Israelites out of Egypt, a major religious figure.

clue.text: One of the European people to work hard, ousting English

indicators.note: ousting means the letter for English is pushed out

parts.note: to slave is to work hard

explanation.surface: A European toils away after driving out an Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Slavs are a group of peoples of eastern Europe, so one is a European person.

clue.text: Accent is to be got right with introduction of Latin hymns

indicators.note: letters that need to be got right are jumbled and must be sorted into order
the introduction of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Pronunciation must be correct when singing Latin hymns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be got right' rearranges ACCENT IS plus L, the first letter of 'Latin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Canticles are hymns or chants with biblical texts, such as the Magnificat, sung in church services.

clue.text: Strength of character after drug trip? The reverse

indicators.note: the reverse says to swap the order the clue gives, so the drug comes after the trip

parts.note: a spin is a short trip, as in a spin in the car
E is short for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone shows backbone after a drug-fuelled outing, or perhaps the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly, 'after drug trip' would put SPIN after E; 'The reverse' flips it so E follows SPIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Spine is used figuratively for backbone, courage or firmness of character.

clue.text: Depression after study then sense getting back to normal

indicators.note: after places the depression behind the word for study

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study
a vale is a valley, a depression in the land
scent is a sense, as of smell

explanation.surface: A depressed student, after much thought, starts to feel normal again.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone convalescent is recovering from illness, gradually returning to health.
